## Vocabulary

## How it works

- [statement] Bybit documents two Filled order messages when cancellation races with execution: one reports execution and the other reports the rejected cancellation. A monitor must not count those status messages as two independent fills. (low confidence) — https://bybit-exchange.github.io/docs/v5/websocket/private/order · keywords: Crypto bot order and position reconciliation
- [statement] NautilusTrader compares net positions per account and instrument using account quantity tolerance. When a venue reports both long and short positions, startup validation requires both side totals to match; equal net quantity alone is insufficient. Strategy ownership can also be ambiguous when several strategies share an account-level net position. (low confidence) — https://nautilustrader.io/docs/latest/concepts/execution/reconciliation/ · keywords: Crypto bot order and position reconciliation
- [statement] A 2022 Freqtrade maintainer reply states that the bot only handled its own orders and did not expect to detect a manually closed position. The maintainer could not diagnose the reported rejection without earlier logs. This is historical scope evidence, not proof of current Freqtrade behavior or a confirmed root cause. (low confidence) — https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/issues/6739 · keywords: Crypto bot order and position reconciliation
- [statement] NautilusTrader startup validation matches hedging positions by exact venue position identity and quantity, and netting positions by account and instrument within account tolerance. When the venue reports both long and short positions, matching only net quantity is insufficient. (low confidence) — https://nautilustrader.io/docs/latest/concepts/execution/reconciliation/ · keywords: Crypto bot order and position reconciliation
- [statement] NautilusTrader caps targeted single-order reconciliation queries per cycle, defers remaining orders, and spaces consecutive queries to avoid venue rate limits. This provides a concrete bounded-query pattern for reconciliation after bulk-query failures. (low confidence) — https://nautilustrader.io/docs/latest/concepts/execution/reconciliation/ · keywords: Crypto bot order and position reconciliation

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] In NautilusTrader Polymarket issue 4787, a reporter reproduced a terminal Filled report with filled quantity below original quantity, leaving the local order pending cancellation. A maintainer confirmed the mapping and required a terminal state while preserving the separate dust-underfill rule. This illustrates why quantity agreement alone cannot validate an adapter status mapping. (low confidence) — https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader/issues/4787 · keywords: Crypto bot order and position reconciliation

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Reconcile orders, fills, and positions separately: NautilusTrader processes venue order and fill reports before checking positions, while Freqtrade updates exchange order state before verifying existing positions. This supports a monitor that compares execution state with venue exposure rather than treating an open-order list as a position ledger. (medium confidence) — https://nautilustrader.io/docs/latest/concepts/execution/reconciliation/ · keywords: Crypto bot order and position reconciliation · also: https://www.freqtrade.io/en/stable/bot-basics/
- [statement] Order status and fill quantity are distinct reconciliation inputs. CCXT describes one order producing multiple fills; Bybit exposes remaining quantity, cumulative executed quantity, and average fill price separately. A monitor should compare executed quantities rather than infer execution volume from status-event counts. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/ccxt/ccxt/wiki/manual · keywords: Crypto bot order and position reconciliation · also: https://bybit-exchange.github.io/docs/v5/websocket/private/order
- [statement] In NautilusTrader, a missing position report, null quantity, or venue without position publication is not evidence of a flat position. A failed position query causes that venue to be skipped for the cycle rather than interpreting absent reports as flat. (low confidence) — https://nautilustrader.io/docs/latest/concepts/execution/reconciliation/ · keywords: Crypto bot order and position reconciliation

## Facts and statements

- [statement] A CCXT RequestTimeout leaves the request outcome unknown. For a createOrder timeout, its manual directs clients to check order history and open/closed orders, then balances if the order is no longer open. Blindly interpreting a timeout as rejection can therefore make a retry unsafe. (low confidence) — https://github.com/ccxt/ccxt/wiki/manual · keywords: Crypto bot order and position reconciliation
- [statement] In NautilusTrader startup reconciliation, an explicit open or flat position report is authoritative; a missing report or null quantity is not evidence of flatness. The documented guarantee applies only to reports included by configured position and instrument filters. (low confidence) — https://nautilustrader.io/docs/latest/concepts/execution/reconciliation/ · keywords: Crypto bot order and position reconciliation
- [statement] A REST snapshot arriving after a streamed fill need not describe newer state. NautilusTrader explicitly warns that response arrival time, equal timestamps, or timestamps from different clocks do not establish that a snapshot includes the fill. A lower cumulative fill total must be distinguished from an explicit fill correction. (low confidence) — https://nautilustrader.io/docs/latest/concepts/execution/reconciliation/ · keywords: Crypto bot order and position reconciliation
- [statement] The reporter of NautilusTrader Derive issue 5355 observed a partial IOC fill arriving after cancellation on crates 0.63.0 with the v2 API. The reporter said position, balance, and PnL appeared correct, but the fill carried reconciliation = true and caused their strategy to pause. Treat this as an attributed historical adapter report, not evidence that every reconciliation fill indicates lost exposure. (low confidence) — https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader/issues/5355 · keywords: Crypto bot order and position reconciliation
- [statement] Freqtrade issue 12681 reports Binance Futures conditional stop orders that could be created but temporarily could not be fetched or cancelled, leading to multiple conditional orders. The maintainer described orders appearing later and said Freqtrade retained their identities. The report scopes an order-not-found response: it did not prove that those conditional orders never existed. (low confidence) — https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade/issues/12681 · keywords: Crypto bot order and position reconciliation
- [statement] NautilusTrader defines reconciliation as aligning internal order and position state with venue state; it performs startup recovery and continuous checks for runtime discrepancies. (low confidence) — https://nautilustrader.io/docs/latest/concepts/execution/reconciliation/ · keywords: Crypto bot order and position reconciliation
- [statement] Cancellation can race with execution. Bybit documents two Filled status messages for one cancel/fill race, and CCXT documents a cancel reaching an already filled order. Treating each terminal-status message as an additional fill would therefore be unsafe. (medium confidence) — https://bybit-exchange.github.io/docs/v5/websocket/private/order · keywords: Crypto bot order and position reconciliation · also: https://github.com/ccxt/ccxt/wiki/manual
- [statement] Reconcile executed quantity separately from terminal status: CCXT says a canceled order may already be partially filled and exposes filled quantity; Bybit exposes cumulative executed quantity and remaining unexecuted quantity. Cancellation does not imply zero execution. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/ccxt/ccxt/wiki/manual · keywords: Crypto bot order and position reconciliation · also: https://bybit-exchange.github.io/docs/v5/websocket/private/order
- [statement] A missing open-order record does not establish a final cancellation outcome. NautilusTrader explicitly notes that open-order endpoints omit closed orders and uses a targeted single-order query before terminal not-found resolution; CCXT also documents missing closed-order endpoint support on some exchanges. (medium confidence) — https://nautilustrader.io/docs/latest/concepts/execution/reconciliation/ · keywords: Crypto bot order and position reconciliation · also: https://github.com/ccxt/ccxt/wiki/manual
- [statement] NautilusTrader generates external order events for unrecognized or absent client order IDs. CCXT supports user clientOrderId only where the exchange supports it. Attribution logic must therefore account for venue capability and orders outside its recognized client IDs. (medium confidence) — https://nautilustrader.io/docs/latest/concepts/execution/reconciliation/ · keywords: Crypto bot order and position reconciliation · also: https://github.com/ccxt/ccxt/wiki/manual

## Research summary — Crypto bot order and position reconciliation

Order and position reconciliation compares local execution records with venue orders, fills, and exposure. The evidence distinguishes unknown request outcomes, duplicated status notifications, late fills, inconsistent adapter mappings, and snapshots that predate streamed executions. NautilusTrader documents separate order, fill, and position checks; Freqtrade documents updating exchange order state before position checks. Historical issue reports show why a monitor must preserve order identity, inspect quantities and terminal states, and qualify what a missing order or position report proves. Reconciliation labels and net position agreement alone do not establish that every execution was classified correctly.
